briefing.headline: OpenAI o4 and DeepSeek R2 ignite new phase of frontier model escalation as compute arms race intensifies

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: Frontier labs released multiple reasoning models this week while US export controls tighten further on advanced chips. Prompt injection attacks continue rising in production deployments across autonomous systems. DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation gains traction as protocol-level defense.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI deployed o4 with native multi-agent orchestration reaching 87% on GPQA. Anthropic released Claude 4 Opus and Meta open-sourced Llama 4 405B variant. DeepSeek R2 now leads Chinese open models on MATH benchmark.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems and that DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level. NIST issued new guidelines for agentic AI sandboxing.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: Microsoft announced $4.2B expansion of its Arizona AI supercluster. TSMC began volume production of 2nm process for next-gen AI accelerators. Google TPU v6 pods now online with 35% efficiency gains.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will regulatory fragmentation between US, EU, and China slow or accelerate the path to AGI-level systems by 2028?
